subject: Known mean of the random field

messages.author: c26aea8d9e280cf7
messages.subject: Known mean of the random field
parts:
Hello,

I'd like some help to figure out how to include mean in Gaussian process in INLA.
Recently, I read SIMPSON's paper 2016, 'Going off grid: Computationally efficient inference for log-Gaussian Cox processes'. It uses inhomogeneous poisson process to model points within a region and assumes Z(s) ~GP(0, C). The code to deal with this problem can be found in INLA tutorial 4.1 (http://inla.r-inla-download.org/r-inla.org/tutorials/spde/html/ ).  

Now in my case, I have a known mean for the Gaussian process, that is Z(s) ~GP(mean(s), C). I wonder how I should change the function or something in INLA code to include mean.

Thanks in advance for helping.

Regards

Mia

messages.author: afb003e064114795
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Known mean of the random field
parts:
Hi, easiest is probably to include the known mean as an offset in the model, either with offset() or by modifying the exposure, E.  In both cases, this requires doing that in a way that works with the LGCP likelihood setup. (Unless you don’t have an LGCP and just referred to that as an example).

I believe, but haven’t tested, that you can simply include the mean as an “effect” named e.g. myprocessmean in the inla.stack call just as you wold for a fixed effect covariate vector, associated with the same A matrix as the GP, and add
+offset(myprocessmean)
to the formula.
However, I’m not sure at what stage offset() is processed internally, so this might not work. If it fails, then I think the inlabru package should be able to do it (it parses the formula in a different way that allows more general R expressions).

Finn
